sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 covers the north end of Penns Grove along the Delaware River, from Borden Avenue at the top to Poplar Street at the bottom and from the river bank east to Morris Avenue. North Riverside Walk follows the shore, lined with rows of small frame dwellings numbered along the walk. Inland from it the blocks are named rows and courts of workers' housing: a row of identical dwellings on the south side of Borden Avenue, a few more along Bowen Alley, the long terrace of Miller's Row, and Wood's Place, a court of small dwellings opening off Denny's Road, which runs down to Denny's Wharf on the river. Delaware Avenue runs up the middle of the sheet; east of it the large blocks 118 and 119 north of West Line Street are almost empty, with only a battery service station near Line. The township line between the borough and Upper Penns Neck Township is drawn across the sheet just north of West Line Street, so the northern half of the sheet lies in the township. South of West Line Street, between Delaware Avenue, Penn Street, Morris Avenue and Poplar Street, are two blocks of frame dwellings with stables, garages and a carpenter shop; a few dwellings are of concrete block. Water pipes of 4 inches run in Delaware Avenue, Penn and Morris with hydrants. Sheet 3 adjoins on the south and sheet 18 on the east. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left; the top right corner holds an inset (part 2) continuing the river front north of Borden Avenue.
notes: Denny's Road is Woods Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Line is West Line Street
Borden Avenue, Bowen Alley and Miller's Row are not in OpenStreetMap; the area north of Line Street has been rebuilt with a new street grid (2nd to 7th Avenue)
Borough limits and the Upper Penns Neck Township line are drawn across the sheet north of West Line

Scale 50 ft. North end along the Delaware River: N. Riverside Walk, Borden Av, Bowen Alley, Millers Row, Dennys Rd, Woods Pl, Delaware Av, W. Line, Penn, Morris, Poplar; Upper Penns Neck Township line crosses it. Two parts: main map and an inset at top right (north side of Borden Av, block 175) inside a heavy line.

sheet-2-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 2 is an inset in the top right corner of the sheet, set off by a heavy line, that continues the river front north of the main map. It shows block 175 on the north side of Borden Avenue between North Riverside Walk and Delaware Avenue, with a stretch of the Delaware River bank on the west. Along the walk stand a few frame dwellings and a pair of two-storey stores lettered A to F; on Borden Avenue a row of four identical frame dwellings faces the row on the south side of the avenue shown on the main map, and there are a few more dwellings, a garage and a stable in the block behind. Most of the block is open ground, and only the near side of Delaware Avenue is drawn, at the right edge. The large numeral 2 below Borden Avenue refers the reader back to the main part of the same sheet. The inset lies in Upper Penns Neck Township, north of the borough line, and is drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main map (50 feet to an inch, north to the upper left). It was placed from four block corners at Borden Avenue that both parts draw, carried from the placement of the main map; no modern street junction falls inside it.
notes: Placed from four block corners carried from part 1; low confidence
Borden Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap; the area has been rebuilt

Scale 50 ft. North end along the Delaware River: N. Riverside Walk, Borden Av, Bowen Alley, Millers Row, Dennys Rd, Woods Pl, Delaware Av, W. Line, Penn, Morris, Poplar; Upper Penns Neck Township line crosses it. Two parts: main map and an inset at top right (north side of Borden Av, block 175) inside a heavy line.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the north-western part of Penns Grove along the Delaware River, which runs down the left edge of the sheet with its shoreline drawn in blue. North Riverside Walk follows the shore. The map is bounded by Poplar Street at the top and West Harmony Street at the bottom, with Delaware Avenue, Penn Street, Morris and New running across the sheet as the long streets. Most of the area is frame dwellings on narrow lots with outbuildings, drawn in yellow with a few brick buildings in pink. In the upper left are four rows of small attached cottages lettered Row A to Row D at Woods Grove, and a short private street, Wykagyl Place, is lined with a terrace of numbered dwellings. At the lower left a block of storage buildings, a feed store with elevator and mill, a wagon shed and a stone building stands beside Barbers Wharf, marked as fire ruins, with the shore and the wharf drawn in blue water. Penns Grove Lodging stands on Penn Street near West Harmony Street, and a church lies on Penn Street south of Denny Avenue. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, which a compass rose near the right edge confirms. Adjoining sheets are numbered 2 at the top and 4 at the right.
notes: Wykagyl Place is marked private and is not named in OpenStreetMap
North Riverside Walk follows the river bank and is not in OpenStreetMap (low confidence on the reading: the lettering is partly along the shore)
Barbers Wharf is lettered 'Fire Ruins'
Penn is today Penn Street; Denny Av. is Denny Avenue; Morris is Morris Avenue
Scale 50 ft. Delaware Av, Penn, New, Denny Av, Morris, Poplar, W. Pitman, W. Harmony by the river; Wykagyl Pl, Woods Grove.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north-central blocks of Penns Grove between Poplar Street at the top and West Harmony Street at the bottom. Morris Street runs down the left edge and New, Turner, Franklin and Lanning Avenue cross the sheet, with West Pitman Street as the main east-west street in the middle and Denny Avenue below it. Dwellings with outbuildings fill most blocks, with some vacant lots along Poplar Street and in the east of the sheet. Near West Pitman Street at Lanning Avenue a bottling works faces the street, and a large vacant, dilapidated frame building is marked near Franklin Street. Mitchner's Terrace is a short row of dwellings off New Street. The West Harmony Public School, drawn in blue, stands in the lower left on a large lot. At the lower right the Pennsylvania Railroad and the West Jersey and Seashore line run past feed and commercial buildings, with a compass rose near the right edge. Water pipes (4 and 6 inch) are marked in most streets. Pearl Street is lettered at the right edge, and Guest Street at the top. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Adjoining sheets are numbered 3 at the left, 5 at the right, 18 at the top and 8 at the bottom.
notes: Turner is today Turner Avenue, Lanning Av. is Lanning Avenue
Mitchner's Terrace is not in OpenStreetMap
The railroad is lettered W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.) on the neighbouring sheets
Scale 50 ft. Poplar, W. Pitman, Franklin, Lanning, Turner, Denny, W. Harmony.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the central north part of Penns Grove between Poplar Street at the top and West Harmony Street at the bottom, from Lanning Avenue on the left to North Broad Street on the right. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the top, with several tracks. West of the tracks are the lumber yard of H. S. Justice and Co., with long dashed lumber piles, and a row of dwellings along Lanning Avenue. East of the tracks West Pitman Street, West Griffith Street and West Harmony Street cross the blocks towards North Broad Street, with Pearl Street near the top. Along West Pitman Street stand a gas works, a coal, hay and feed dealer, a cement block factory and, near North Broad Street, a bakery and bake house with storage. A long terrace of attached dwellings lines West Griffith Street, and Penns Grove Public School stands near West Harmony Street and North Broad. East Pitman Street, East Griffith Street and East Harmony Street are lettered at the right edge where sheet 6 continues. A compass rose with a north arrow pointing to the upper left stands near the top. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are numbered 4 at the left, 6 at the right and 9 at the bottom.
notes: Elvin Av. at the top right is Elvin Avenue in OpenStreetMap, which merges the Pearl, Elvin and North Broad junction into one node although the sheet draws the two streets offset
The railroad is lettered W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.)
Gas works are marked 'not in use' (reading medium confidence)
Scale 50 ft. Poplar, Pearl, W. Pitman, Lanning, W. Harmony; W.J.&S. railroad diagonally across.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the east side of North Broad Street in Penns Grove, from Elvin Avenue at the top to East Harmony Street at the bottom, with Barber Avenue as the long street on the right. North Broad Street runs down the left edge, where the sheet joins sheet 5. East Pitman Street and East Griffith Street are drawn running east from Broad Street towards Barber Avenue but are lettered 'not opened' beyond the first blocks, so the right two thirds of the sheet is mostly blank blocks with property lines only. Dwellings and a few stores line North Broad Street, including a garage with heated cement-floor building at the lower left and another garage near the top, and a tile building. The New Jersey Milk Product Company's milk depot stands inside the block between East Pitman Street and East Griffith Street. The Penns Grove Tabernacle, the First Church of Christ, Scientist, and a row of dwellings face East Harmony Street at the bottom. Houses along Elvin Avenue are numbered at the top. A cemetery is lettered at the right edge. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the upper right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Adjoining sheets are numbered 5 at the left, 18 at the top and 10 at the bottom.
notes: East Pitman Street and East Griffith Street are marked 'not opened' east of the first block; the modern node at Barber Avenue and East Pitman Street is about 11 m off the drawn position and was rejected
Elvin Av. is Elvin Avenue today
Reading of the milk depot lettering is medium confidence
Scale 50 ft. N. Broad, Elvin Av, E. Pitman, E. Griffith, E. Harmony, Barber Av.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 covers the old river landing of Penns Grove, from West Harmony Street at the top to the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad yard at the bottom, and from the Delaware River bank east to Oak Street. Delaware Avenue runs along the shore and Penn Street parallel to it; West Main Street comes down to the river at the head of the Wilson Line Pier, the steamboat pier whose landward end is drawn here running out into the river at the left edge. Barbers Wharf, marked as fire ruins, is at the top left. Around the foot of West Main are the Riverside Theatre (motion pictures, closed), a trolley waiting room, the Olympia Hotel, Sickler's Hotel with a club, a bank, offices and a row of stores and halls. The north side of West Main between Penn and Oak is a solid row of stores, dwellings, an auto service station and a tin shop. North of it, toward West Harmony, are frame dwellings, a milk depot and an upholstery shop. South of Main the lumber yard of R. F. Willis and Bro. Inc. fills most of the block toward the railroad, with lumber piles, a cement house, coal bins, a warehouse and a private garage, and a row of buildings marked not in use along the river bank. The railroad tracks and a long platform run across the bottom right, with Railroad Avenue and Airy Street lettered at the edge, and South Riverside Walk starts at the river below the yard. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left. The bottom left corner holds a separate inset (part 2) of the outer end of the pier.
notes: Railroad printed as W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.)
Airy Street is Airy Avenue in OpenStreetMap
Riverside Theatre marked closed; Barbers Wharf marked fire ruins
R. F. Willis and Bro. Inc. lumber yard south of West Main

Scale 50 ft. Delaware Av, Penn, Oak, W. Harmony, W. Main by the river, Wilson Line Pier, rail yard. Two parts: main map and an inset at bottom left (end of the Wilson Line Pier and freight house) at another rotation, inside a heavy line.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: outer end of the Wilson Line Pier with waiting rooms and freight house, in the Delaware River (no street junction or modern feature; drawn at another rotation and the length of pier left out between the main map and the inset is not known; needs a modern pier outline or an aerial photograph of the pier head).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 shows the centre of Penns Grove south of West Harmony Street, with West Main Street as the business street across the middle and the railroad yard along the bottom. Franklin Street divides the upper part of the sheet; Oak Street lies at the left edge and Naylor Avenue at the right. North of West Main Street are dwellings and St. Paul's M.E. Church. West Main Street itself is lined with stores, a printing shop, the Masonic Hall, the Penn Dress Manufacturing Company, a hotel (the Colonial Hotel with lodge rooms above) and other commercial buildings. South of it lie a lumber yard, hardware and paint stores, planing and ice works (the Atlantic Ice Manufacturing Company) and the Russian Caviar Canning Works, marked closed, near Naylor Avenue. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) crosses the lower part of the sheet with many tracks, a passenger depot, a freight depot and a long covered platform, and a railroad tool house. Railroad Avenue runs along the bottom, with Airy Street, Simpkins Place and Mill Street ending on it. A compass rose stands in the lower right. Water pipes are marked in most streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Airy St. is Airy Avenue in OpenStreetMap
Naylor Av. is Naylor Avenue today
The Colonial Hotel and Russian Caviar Canning Works are lettered on the sheet (closed)
Lettering of the lumber yard and ice works is medium confidence
Scale 50 ft. W. Main, Oak, Franklin, Naylor, W. Harmony; W.J.&S. railroad station and yard.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the centre of Penns Grove, the blocks between West Harmony Street on the north and Railroad Avenue on the south, from the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) at the north-west corner to North and South Broad Street on the east, with State Street and Naylor Avenue as the cross streets. West Main Street crosses the middle of the sheet and is the business street: its frontage is lined with stores, auto service stations, a bakery with portable ovens, a plumbing shop, offices and dwellings, and on its south side stands the fire department and borough hall. The Elks Hall is on the north side of West Main. The Penns Grove High School, a large brick building heated by steam, occupies the corner of West Harmony and North Broad. The 1st Baptist Church stands on State Street south of Main. The south-east corner along South Broad has a row of brick and frame stores, a block of concrete-block buildings and a filling station. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings with outbuildings and private garages on long narrow lots running back from Harmony and Main. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets with hydrants. The railroad crosses the north-west corner on a diagonal and the sheet edge beyond it is left open. Short stubs of East Harmony Street, Philips Street, East Main Street and Mary Street are lettered just across Broad at the right edge, where sheet 10 continues. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left.
notes: Railroad printed as W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.)
Philips Street, east of North Broad, is not in OpenStreetMap today
Fire department and borough hall on West Main Street
Scale 50 ft. Pilot. W. Harmony, W. Main, Railroad Av, Naylor Av, State, N. and S. Broad; High School, Elks Hall, Borough Hall.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers the east side of the centre of Penns Grove, from East Harmony Street at the top to Mary Street at the bottom, between North and South Broad Street on the left and Barber Avenue and Cumberland Avenue on the right. East Main Street leaves Broad Street at the centre left and runs diagonally to the lower right, its blocks turned to follow it, while Philips Street and Bowen Terrace branch off in the upper left. Along Broad Street the sheet shows the Post Office, Peoples Bank, The Broad Theatre, a lunch car and a row of stores, with a vulcanizing shop and a garage. Dwellings with outbuildings fill the blocks along East Main Street, with John Street, Mary Street and Cumberland Avenue running off it. In the upper right a large block holds a greenhouse, a dress manufactory and a public school beside Barber Avenue, marked Justice, and a compass rose with a north arrow stands in the upper middle. Lincoln Avenue is lettered at the lower right. Street widths of 33 to 50 feet are lettered along the streets. Several streets are shown running into blocks with property lines only. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Adjoining sheets are numbered 6 at the top, 9 at the left, 12 and 13 at the bottom and 14 at the right.
notes: Philips Street, east of North Broad, is not in OpenStreetMap
Bowen Terrace is not in OpenStreetMap
The modern Barber Avenue and East Main Street junction is not drawn on the sheet and was excluded
Reading of 'Barber Av. (Justice)' is medium confidence; the bracketed word is lettered under the street name
Lettering of the dress manufactory is low confidence
Scale 50 ft. E. Harmony, E. Main, S. Broad, Mary St, Philips St east of Broad.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the south-west edge of Penns Grove along the Delaware River, from Railroad Avenue on the north to Beach Avenue on the south, with Naylor Avenue running down the right edge. On the left the river shore is lined by South Riverside Walk, a street of small frame dwellings, most with porches, built in close rows on narrow lots between the walk and the water. Airy Street, Simpkins Place and Mill Street run back from Railroad Avenue into blocks 70 and 71, which hold dwellings, small stores, a private gymnasium and a small brick-built (pink) building group beside Mill Street. A single dwelling stands apart on the shore below the first row of houses, and a second row of dwellings continues down South Riverside Walk to Beach Avenue. The middle of the sheet, block 76, is open land. The Pennsylvania Railroad (West Jersey and Seashore) runs north to south through the right half on a curve with several tracks, with a siding at the top. Near the bottom right the J. J. Myers coal yard occupies both sides of the tracks, with coal piles, a soap works warehouse and an office. Beach Avenue crosses the bottom with a row of dwellings on its north side and more on the south side beside a private driveway. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in Railroad and Beach Avenues. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left, and the compass rose is in the middle.
notes: Airy Street is Airy Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Simpkins Place keeps its name
Mill Street continues south to Beach Avenue in OpenStreetMap but the sheet draws it only as far as the shore turn
Modern streets along the shore (Delaware Drive, Spruce Street, Cedar Road) are later and were not matched to South Riverside Walk

Placed from four control points, two hand-picked on Railroad Avenue and two near the Naylor Avenue edge; the lower left has no control. A railroad crossing was left out because the modern track lies about 19 m from the drawn one
Control lies on the north and east edges only (Railroad Avenue and Naylor Avenue); the shore is extrapolated

Scale 50 ft. Riverfront south of the rail yard: S. Riverside Walk, Airy St, Simpkins Pl, Mill St, Railroad Av, Beach Av, Naylor Av. Control only on the north (Railroad Av) and east (Naylor Av) edges; the shore is extrapolated. Lead replaced the detected Beach / Naylor (placed 50 ft east: Naylor east edge taken for a boundary) with a hand pick and added Naylor / Sack.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 shows the blocks south of the town centre between Railroad Avenue on the north and Beach Avenue on the south, from Naylor Avenue on the west to South Broad Street on the east, with State Street dividing the sheet into two columns of blocks and Sack Avenue crossing the middle. The blocks are numbered 72, 73, 74A and 74B. The eastern column along South Broad Street is the most built up, with rows of brick and frame stores on the west side of South Broad, a furniture store, a warehouse, a garage and dwellings with outbuildings. North of Sack Avenue the west column has dwellings and a garage with a capacity for 18 cars, and the rest of block 72 is open ground. South of Sack Avenue the west blocks hold the vacant Oxford Hotel at the Beach Avenue corner and a few dwellings, while the east blocks have dwellings and private garages. Below Beach Avenue, at the bottom edge, stand the Hotel Francis (boarding) and St. James School (R.C.), a pink brick building heated by steam. Short stubs of Mary Street, Mitchell Avenue and Walnut Street are lettered across South Broad at the right edge, where sheet 13 continues. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches run in the streets with hydrants. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north is to the upper left; the compass rose is on the left.
notes: Sack Avenue and the blocks on both sides of State Street south of Railroad Avenue are open ground in places
Streets keep their names in OpenStreetMap; Naylor Avenue is the western edge of the sheet and also the right edge of sheet 11
Twelve control points, all detected; the fit rests on streets across the whole sheet
Scale 50 ft. Railroad Av, Naylor, State, Sack Av, Beach Av, S. Broad.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 lies east of South Broad Street, which runs down the left edge, and extends from Mary Street on the north to Willis Street on the south and east to Cumberland Avenue. The blocks are numbered 75, 76, 77, 88, 79 and 17A to 17C. Mitchell Avenue and Walnut Street cross it from west to east, Tyron Avenue and Westminster Avenue run north and south through it, and John Street and Lincoln Avenue run obliquely in the upper right where the street grid turns toward East Main Street. Along South Broad are stores, lodge rooms, a garage with a capacity for 12 cars, another larger garage with a capacity for 20 cars, and several tile buildings, drawn in pink, with brick kilns and a vacant stores building. The rest is frame dwellings with outbuildings on narrow lots, many divided by 10 foot alleys. Tyron Avenue is marked not opened between Mitchell Avenue and Walnut Street. The east side, between Westminster and Cumberland Avenues, is laid out in long narrow lots, mostly unbuilt, with two tile buildings near Walnut Street. Stubs of Sack Avenue and Beach Avenue appear at the left edge west of South Broad. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in Mary Street and South Broad. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left, and the compass rose is at the right.
notes: Tyron Avenue is Tyrone Avenue in OpenStreetMap
Westminster Avenue is Westminister Avenue in OpenStreetMap
Mary, Walnut and Willis are drawn without a suffix; today they are Mary Street, Walnut Street and Willis Avenue
Eleven control points, all detected, leave-one-out about 1.2 m
Scale 50 ft. S. Broad, Mitchell Av, Walnut, Willis, Tyrone, Cumberland area.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the area where East Main Street runs diagonally across the sheet from the upper left to the lower right, between Cumberland Avenue on the west and the Trumbull Avenue district on the east. North of East Main the blocks are numbered 63, 65 and 181 (12) and hold dwellings, stores, tile buildings and a number of barns and outbuildings along the main road, with North Smith Avenue running up the sheet from East Main. South of East Main, Lincoln Avenue, South Smith Avenue and Cumberland Avenue form oblique blocks in blocks 65, 66 and 67, which hold dwellings and lots running back from the main road. Further south the grid turns square again: Walnut Street runs across the lower part, with Deming Avenue and Virginia Avenue crossing it and the blocks numbered 66, 79, 80, 81 and 82 laid out in long narrow lots with some dwellings, a bakery and its oven, and St. Stephens U.A.M.E. Church south of the main road. Trumbull Avenue runs obliquely in the east, with Maryland Avenue and New Jersey Avenue leaving it to the east; block 69 and blocks 67 and 68 are mostly open land. Water pipes of 4 inches are marked in East Main Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left, and the compass rose is at the upper right.
notes: Trumbull Avenue is Trumble Avenue in OpenStreetMap
East Main Street east of Virginia Avenue is Harding Highway today
Walnut Street is drawn about 30 ft wide at its east end against 50 ft in the parcels
The Walnut / Virginia / Trumbull junction was left out of the fit (3.6 m residual, two modern nodes 20 m apart)
Nine control points, all detected, leave-one-out about 1.9 m
Scale 50 ft. E. Main, Walnut, Cumberland, Lincoln, Deming, Trumbull, Virginia area.

sheet-15-1.description: The main part of sheet 15 covers the eastern edge of Penns Grove along East Main Street, from Laurel Street east past Norman Avenue to Alden Avenue, and from Halstead Avenue, lettered as not opened, at the top to Herold Street at the bottom, with Maryland Avenue crossing the middle. The township line between the borough and Upper Penns Neck Township enters at the top, crosses diagonally to East Main Street and then runs down the sheet between Norman and Alden Avenues, so the eastern blocks lie in the township. This is a thinly built suburban district: the blocks, numbered 104 and 113 to 117 and 182 to 185, are divided into lots but carry only scattered frame dwellings, a few garages, a cooper shop and a small shop, with much of the ground still empty. A blue concrete-block garage stands in block 113. No water pipes or hydrants are shown in these streets. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, at a steeper angle than the sheets of the old town. A strip at the bottom left, set off by a heavy line, is a separate part (part 2) showing East Main Street farther west, between Trumbull Avenue and Laurel Street.
notes: East Main Street is Harding Highway in OpenStreetMap here
Laurel is Torton Avenue, Alden Avenue is North and South Miller Avenue, Herold is Harold Street, Norman Avenue is Norman Avenue and South Norman Avenue in OpenStreetMap

sheet-15-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 15 is a strip in the bottom left corner of the sheet, set off from the main map by a heavy line, that carries East Main Street farther west than the main map reaches. It shows the blocks on both sides of East Main between Trumbull Avenue at the left edge and Laurel Street at the right. North of Main, block 111 is taken up by the planing mill of Alfred Gillison: a planing mill and warehouse, lumber sheds, a cement and earth warehouse, an office with a dwelling, and a few small sheds; the note under it gives a night watchman, no clock, electric power and lights, stove heat and chemical extinguishers with sand pails. The rest of the block has a few dwellings and garages. South of Main, block 68 has four frame dwellings and garages facing the street. The large numeral 15 beside Laurel refers to the main part of the same sheet, where Laurel and East Main meet again at its left edge. The strip is drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main map, 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left, and it holds the sheet's scale bar.
notes: East Main Street is Harding Highway, Trumbull Avenue is Trumble Avenue and Laurel is Torton Avenue in OpenStreetMap
Placed from two junctions (helmert); scale and rotation agree with part 1 within 0.5 percent and 0.1 degree

Scale 50 ft. E. Main (Harding Highway), Laurel (now Torton Av), Norman, Alden (now Miller Av), Halstead, Maryland, Herold; township line. Two parts: main map and a strip at bottom left inside a heavy line (E. Main between Trumbull and Laurel, Gillison planing mill).

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the south-west riverfront of Penns Grove, between the Delaware River and State Street, from the blocks above West Church Street at the top to a private way at the bottom. Most of the sheet is the large open block 16, crossed diagonally by the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad branch to the Du Pont plant, with only a few garages, a stable and a row of small frame dwellings lettered B to G east of it. The built-up part is the river edge: South Riverside Walk follows the shore down the whole left side and turns east along the south, lined with small frame dwellings, many with sleeping porches, a grocery, a club and a few stables, with a private driveway behind the upper row. West Church Street crosses the top of the sheet from the walk to State Street, with dwellings on both sides east of the railroad, a concrete-block garage and the edge of a brick building at the top right. State Street runs down the right edge and continues south as State (Eden), and a private way at the bottom leads from it toward the river past a row of identical dwellings. A 6 inch water pipe and a hydrant are shown in State Street. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the upper left; adjoining sheets are 11 and 12 above and 17 to the right and below.
notes: Railroad printed as W. J. & S. R. R. (to Du Pont Plant) P. R. R.; today the Penns Grove Secondary
West Church is Church Street in OpenStreetMap; State (Eden) is State Street south of Church

Placed from Church / State, the railroad crossing of State, two corners of St. James School carried from sheet 12 and a corner at Private Way carried from sheet 17; the riverfront has no control of its own: low to medium confidence

The river side has no control of its own.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 is the south end of Penns Grove, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, and shows the strip along South Broad Street from Beach Avenue and Willis at the top to Bay and West Maple Avenue at the Delaware River, with the town cemetery and the open ground behind it. At the top left, State Street, West Church Street and Beach Avenue enclose blocks of dwellings; the Emmanuel M.E. Church with its horse shed stands beside the cemetery on the west side of South Broad. East of South Broad is a long cemetery and, along East Church Street, a large greenhouse range with sheds and a coal shed. The grid east of Westminster Avenue is laid out in long narrow lots for blocks 90, 91, 93 and 94, with Diver Avenue, Cumberland Avenue, South Smith Avenue, Park Avenue and Iona Avenue, mostly not opened, and Zion Circle drawn as a traffic circle at the east edge. The railroad (W. J. & S. R. R.) crosses the sheet from upper left to lower right. At the south the town is built up along South Broad, West and East Maple Avenue, River Street, Bay and Bay View, with an apartment building at the river and a Du Pont water system marked. In the south-east are the electric substation, Summerill Avenue, Church Street, Shell Road and the Episcopal church; a note says these blocks are also shown on the Carneys Point map and the borough limit crosses the bottom.
notes: State Street is printed State (Eden); Eden is the name of the district
Tyron Avenue is Tyrone Avenue and Westminster Avenue is Westminister Avenue in OpenStreetMap

Park, Iona, Zion Circle and the streets east of Cumberland are marked not opened and do not survive as drawn
The fitted rotation is about -39 degrees, matching the north arrow on this sheet, 11 degrees more than sheets 13 to 15

Maple, River, Bay View, Summerill, Shell Rd, Cypress; drawn turned further than its neighbours (fitted -39 degrees, as its north arrow); blocks also shown on the Carneys Point map.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the north-east edge of Penns Grove and the adjoining part of Upper Penns Neck Township, drawn at the smaller scale of 100 feet to an inch. West Line Street crosses the sheet from Morris at the left edge past Turner, Guest, Lanning Avenue and Wright to the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, and Poplar runs parallel to it below; the borough and township line follows West Line. East of the railroad, North Broad runs up the sheet with East Line, West and East Union, Pearl and Elvin Avenue meeting it. The blocks between Morris and Wright, numbered 120 to 129B, are laid out in narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings, and the Bishop Russell's Memorial A.M.E. Church stands on West Line at Lanning. Along North Broad, both above and below East Line, is a denser row of dwellings, and a synagogue stands near Elvin Avenue. In the north-east, Friendship Avenue follows the railroad, whose Friendship Station is drawn beside the tracks; beyond it Farm Road leads off to the east. At the top are the Standard Oil Co. plant with its tanks, fireproof concrete buildings built in 1927 and a pump house, the W. Borden milk depot, and an 8 inch water pipe in North Broad leading to the pumping station. A stand pipe of 93,000 gallons, 110 feet high, stands east of North Broad. Large areas of the sheet, especially the north-west, are open ground with only lot lines. North points to the upper left.
notes: Railroad printed as W. J. & S. R. R. (P. R. R.)
Friendship Avenue is lettered arbitrary, probably for arbitrary house numbers
Standard Oil Co. buildings marked fireproof construction, built 1927
West Union and East Union meet North Broad about 20 ft apart on the sheet, as the two modern nodes do
